---
id: cpp-ps-pivot-and-split
title: Pivot Index and Three Equal Parts
difficulty: Medium
order: 5
tags: prefix sums, counting, arrays
time_limit: 1
---
## Statement
```cpp
int pivot_index(const std::vector<long long>& a);
    // the LEFTMOST i where sum(a[0..i-1]) == sum(a[i+1..n-1]); -1 if none
long long ways_three_parts(const std::vector<long long>& a);
    // number of ways to cut a into three NON-EMPTY contiguous parts with equal sums
```

`[1,7,3,6,5,6]` has pivot index 3 (1+7+3 = 5+6 = 11). `[0,0,0,0]` can be split 3 ways: `|0|0|00`, `|0|00|0` and `|00|0|0`.

For the pivot, the left sum is a running prefix, and the right sum is `total − left − a[i]`.

For three parts, the total must be divisible by 3. The first cut ends where the prefix equals `T/3`, and the second cut ends where the prefix equals `2T/3`, with at least one element between the cuts and after the second. Count the pairs in one pass: when you reach a valid second cut, add the number of valid first cuts **strictly before it**.

**Input:** cases until the end of input: `n` + values (n ≤ 10⁶, |a[i]| ≤ 10⁹).

## Starter
```cpp
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

int pivot_index(const vector<long long>& a) { return -1; }
long long ways_three_parts(const vector<long long>& a) { return 0; }
```

## Driver
```cpp
int main() {
    ios::sync_with_stdio(false); cin.tie(nullptr);
    int n;
    while (cin >> n) {
        vector<long long> a(n);
        for (auto& x : a) cin >> x;
        cout << pivot_index(a) << ' ' << ways_three_parts(a) << '\n';
    }
}
```

129692 0

## Hints
- Pivot: right sum = total − left sum − a[i]. No second array is needed.
- Three parts: the total must be divisible by 3. Part 1 ends where the prefix is T/3, and part 2 ends where it is 2T/3.
- Scan once, counting the valid first cuts seen so far. When you hit a valid second cut (not the last index), add that count. Be careful when T = 0.

## Solution
**Pivot.** `left` is the sum of `a[0..i−1]`. The right side is everything else except `a[i]`: `total − left − a[i]`. One pass, O(1) per index.

**Three parts.** Let `pre(i)` be the sum of `a[0..i]`. A split is a pair `i < j` with `pre(i) = T/3` (the end of part 1), `pre(j) = 2T/3` (the end of part 2), and `j ≤ n − 2` (part 3 is non-empty).

Scan `j` from left to right. When `pre(j) = 2T/3`, every first cut `i < j` with `pre(i) = T/3` forms a valid split. Counting those as you go makes it O(n).

The order of the two `if`s matters when `T = 0`. Then `T/3 = 2T/3 = 0`, and an index must not serve as both cuts at once. So it's added to `firstCuts` only *after* being considered as a second cut.

Complexity: O(n) time, O(1) space.

```cpp
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

int pivot_index(const vector<long long>& a) {
    long long total = accumulate(a.begin(), a.end(), 0LL), left = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < (int)a.size(); ++i) {
        if (left == total - left - a[i]) return i;
        left += a[i];
    }
    return -1;
}

long long ways_three_parts(const vector<long long>& a) {
    int n = a.size();
    long long total = accumulate(a.begin(), a.end(), 0LL);
    if (n < 3 || total % 3 != 0) return 0;
    long long third = total / 3, pre = 0, firstCuts = 0, ways = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i + 1 < n; ++i) {          // i = last index of the second part (needs a third part after it)
        pre += a[i];
        if (pre == 2 * third && i >= 1) ways += firstCuts;   // pairs with every earlier valid first cut
        if (pre == third) ++firstCuts;         // i can end the first part (counted AFTER, so cuts differ)
    }
    return ways;
}
```
